ai.literal: Wealth / those who are not / as worthy / makes / wealth / other than / there is no / wealth.
ai.translation: There is nothing of real value other than wealth, which turns even worthless people into people of worth.
ai.modern: ஒரு பொருட்டாக மதிக்கத்தகாதவர்களையும் மதிக்கத்தக்கவர்களாகச் செய்யும் செல்வத்தைத் தவிர, உலகில் சிறந்த பொருள் வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the transformative power of wealth in society. The word 'poruḷ' is used repeatedly here to mean both material wealth and intrinsic worth or significance. It states that wealth can elevate even those who lack personal merit into people of importance. Therefore, apart from such wealth, there is no other substance of true practical value in the world.

ai.literal: Those without, everyone will despise; the wealthy, everyone will do honor.
ai.translation: Everyone despises those without wealth, but everyone honors the wealthy.
ai.modern: பொருள் இல்லாதவரை உலகத்தார் அனைவரும் இகழ்வார்கள். ஆனால் செல்வம் உடையவரை அனைவரும் மதித்துச் சிறப்பு செய்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the societal treatment of the poor and the wealthy. The word illārai literally means those who do not have, which in this chapter's context specifically refers to those without wealth. The verb eḷḷuvar indicates mockery or contempt, showing how society looks down upon poverty. Conversely, ciṟappu means special honor or greatness, which everyone readily offers to celvarai, the wealthy. The repetition of ellārum, meaning everyone, emphasizes that this is a universal human tendency.

ai.literal: Wealth which is called unfailing lamp darkness will destroy intended to the land having gone.
ai.translation: The unfailing lamp called wealth will travel to whatever land one intends and dispel the darkness there.
ai.modern: பொருள் என்று சொல்லப்படும் அணையாத விளக்கு, ஒருவர் நினைத்த நாட்டிற்குச் சென்று அங்குள்ள இருளைப் போக்கும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet metaphorically describes wealth as an unfailing lamp. Unlike a physical lamp that stays in one place and can be extinguished, the lamp of wealth can travel to any land its owner desires. Once there, it dispels the darkness of poverty, helplessness, or enmity. The word 'பொய்யா' (unfailing) emphasizes that wealth is a reliable tool that consistently achieves the intended results across borders.

ai.literal: Virtue it will yield, happiness and it will yield, proper means having known, evil without, that came wealth.
ai.translation: Wealth acquired through proper means and without doing evil will yield both virtue and happiness.
ai.modern: சரியான வழியை அறிந்து தீமை இல்லாமல் சேர்க்கப்பட்ட செல்வம் ஒருவனுக்கு அறத்தையும் தரும் இன்பத்தையும் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the dual benefits of wealth earned righteously. When a person accumulates wealth by knowing the proper methods and avoiding evil deeds, that wealth becomes a source of good. It yields virtue because it can be used for righteous deeds, and it yields happiness by providing a good life free from guilt. The repetition of the word yield emphasizes that both outcomes naturally flow from pure wealth.

ai.literal: With compassion and with love that-does-not-come wealth accumulation, without-embracing, to roll-away let-go.
ai.translation: Do not embrace the accumulation of wealth that does not come with compassion and love; let it slip away.
ai.modern: அருளும் அன்பும் இல்லாமல் சேரும் செல்வத்தை ஏற்றுக்கொள்ளாமல், அது தன்னை விட்டுப் போகும்படி விட்டுவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet advises against acquiring wealth through ruthless or unethical means. 'Arul' (compassion) and 'anbu' (love) are the necessary companions of righteous wealth. If wealth is accumulated without these qualities, the text instructs the seeker not to embrace it ('pullar'), but rather to let it roll away ('purala vidal'). True prosperity must align with human kindness.

ai.literal: Accrued wealth and toll wealth and his foes' conquered wealth are the king's wealth.
ai.translation: Wealth that accrues on its own, wealth collected as tolls, and wealth captured by defeating foes constitute the king's treasury.
ai.modern: தானாக வந்து சேரும் பொருளும், சுங்க வரியாக வரும் பொருளும், தன் பகைவரை வென்று பெறும் பொருளும் அரசனுக்கு உரிய பொருள்களாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet lists the three legitimate sources of revenue for a state. The first is wealth that accrues naturally, such as ownerless property or natural resources. The second is wealth collected through tolls and customs duties. The third is wealth acquired by defeating enemies in battle. Together, these form the treasury of a king.

ai.literal: Hill having climbed elephant battle like seeing, one's own hand something to be he who does action.
ai.translation: Undertaking a venture with one's own wealth in hand is like safely watching an elephant battle from a hilltop.
ai.modern: தன் கையில் சொந்தப் பொருள் இருக்க ஒரு செயலைத் தொடங்குவது, ஒருவன் பாதுகாப்பான குன்றின் மேல் ஏறி நின்று யானைப் போரை வேடிக்கை பார்ப்பதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of financial independence when undertaking a project. Just as a person standing on a high hill can safely watch a fierce battle between elephants without fear of getting trampled, a person who uses their own wealth to fund an enterprise can execute it with confidence. Relying on one's own resources removes the anxiety and risks associated with depending on others.

ai.literal: Make wealth; foes' pride severing weapon, than that sharper thing there is not.
ai.translation: Acquire wealth. There is no sharper weapon than that to sever the arrogance of your foes.
ai.modern: பொருளைச் சேருங்கள். பகைவர்களின் செருக்கை அறுக்கக்கூடிய ஆயுதம் அதைவிடக் கூர்மையானது வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The couplet advises one to actively accumulate wealth. It describes wealth metaphorically as a sharp weapon (எஃகு) that cuts down the pride of enemies. The word எஃகு primarily means steel or a bladed weapon, emphasizing that financial strength is the most effective and piercing tool to defeat opposition.

ai.literal: Bright wealth to grow firm to those who have made, easy thing the other two also together.
ai.translation: To those who have firmly accumulated excellent wealth, the other two goals of life are easy to attain together.
ai.modern: சிறந்த பொருளை மிகுதியாகச் சேர்த்தவர்களுக்கு, மற்ற இரண்டுமாகிய அறமும் இன்பமும் எளிதில் ஒருசேரக் கிடைக்கும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet states that acquiring wealth makes the other two goals of life, virtue and pleasure, easily attainable. 'ஒண்பொருள்' refers to excellent or rightfully earned wealth. 'காழ்ப்ப' means to grow firm or abundant, emphasizing the solid accumulation of this wealth. When wealth is secured, 'ஏனை இரண்டும்' (the other two) naturally follow 'ஒருங்கு' (together) without much difficulty.
